purpose: Verify the ATK Token Meter's ACCUMULATOR. Every usage block here is synthetic.
hard_caveat: These are not provider-reported numbers. Nothing in this fixture says anything about any real provider's tokenizer or billing. It tests ATK's arithmetic over usage blocks, which is a real and checkable property, and it tests nothing else. The meter-versus-provider comparison required by METER_CALIBRATION_v1.0.0.md is a separate question that needs a benchmark credential and has NOT been answered.
expectations_provenance: Every 'expected' value was computed by explicit arithmetic in the fixture generator, not by running the meter. 'cost_working' shows the per-call arithmetic so a reviewer can check it by hand.

cases.description: Baseline: one accepted call, no cache, no retry. If this fails, nothing else matters.
Three attempts, the first two rejected. Quantity 6: retry tokens are counted, never discarded.
cases.adversarial_against: a meter that records only the accepted call would report 9,800 input instead of 28,200 - a 65% undercount, and it would look plausible

cases.description: 90% of input served from cache. Quantity 3: cached tokens are reported separately and priced at the cached rate, never folded into input.
cases.adversarial_against: a meter that prices all 40,000 input tokens at the uncached rate reports $0.028182 instead of $0.005214 - a 5.41x overstatement on this call

cases.description: Cheap model attempted, rejected, escalated to the expensive one. Quantity 7: escalation tokens are attributed to the model escalated TO, and each call is priced at its own rate.
cases.adversarial_against: a meter applying one run-level rate would price all 22,600 input tokens at whichever model it picked, and would hide that the escalation is where the money went

cases.description: Everything at once: two cached retries on a cheap model, then an uncached escalation. The realistic shape of a failing-then-recovering run.
cases.adversarial_against: any meter that handles retry, cache and escalation correctly in isolation but loses one of them when they interact

cases.description: One run spanning two providers. Totals must still be correct, AND the comparability guard must fire: cross-provider token deltas are not reportable.
cases.adversarial_against: reporting '8,000 vs 8,000 input tokens, identical efficiency' across two different tokenizers - the numbers match and the comparison is meaningless
